title: Visualizing modified spin-wave wavefronts near magnetic defects and domains using nitrogen-vacancy centers
authors: Wenxin Cheng, Chang Liu, Dekun Shen, Jiaxin Li, Shangyuan Wang, Hongyu Wang, Miming Cai, Jihao Xia, Peng Chen, Caihua Wan, Ka Shen, Xiufeng Han, Yuelin Zhang, Jinxing Zhang, Yangmu Li
abstract: Direct, real-space imaging of spin-wave propagation and wavefronts in magnetic materials is crucial for advancing both fundamental understanding of spin dynamics and the development of functional devices. This, however, remains a significant challenge, especially in materials with complex magnetic characteristics at the nanoscale. Here, we employ scanning nitrogen-vacancy center spectroscopy to achieve visualization of spin waves in two archetypical magnetic films: yttrium-iron-garnet and lanthanum strontium manganese oxide. We reveal a wavelength-dependent spin-wave filtering effect near point-like magnetic scatterers and a modified spin wavefront in antiferromagnetically coupled stripe domains. The spin-wave characteristics are explained using micromagnetic simulations and analytical calculations. These findings point to possible fine control of spin-wave propagation near complex magnetic structures and extend the scope of spin-wave imaging based on nitrogen-vacancy centers beyond uniform magnets.
summary: The research demonstrates the use of nitrogen-vacancy center spectroscopy to visualize spin waves in complex magnetic materials like YIG and LSMO. By analyzing PL contrast and applying advanced phase retrieval techniques, the authors mapped unique phenomena such as wavelength-dependent filtering and characteristic zig-zag wavefront distortions near magnetic domains. This advances spintronics by enabling fine control over spin wave propagation near structural defects.
main_problem: Direct, real-space imaging of spin-wave propagation and wavefronts in magnetic materials with complex nanoscale structures is challenging.
main_result: The study successfully visualized wavelength-dependent filtering effects near scatterers and observed modified, zig-zagging spin wave wavefronts within antiferromagnetically coupled stripe domains.
method: Scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spectroscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations was used to map local magnetic fields and spin-wave phase structure.
model_or_system: The system involves spin waves in archetypal magnetic films like YIG and LSMO, exhibiting complex domain structures stabilized by interactions like the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The measurement relies on NV center resonance spectroscopy.
key_observables: PL contrast, local spin-wave phase (extracted via Riesz transform), field shifts ($\pm 7$ G), and wavefront bending/modification.
important_parameters: Wavelength dependence of scattering effects; comparison between uniform vs. patterned magnetic media; external magnetic fields controlling resonance frequencies.
main_assumptions: The standard PL contrast equation neglects continuous laser pumping effects, and phase extraction in inhomogeneous backgrounds requires advanced techniques like the Riesz transform.
figures_summary: Figures show spin-wave PL contrast images in YIG and LSMO; Figure 2 illustrates wavefront bending near point scatterers; Figure 3 details domain structure analysis in LSMO using frequency scans and Riesz transforms; Figure 4 presents micromagnetic simulations of magnetization and dispersion relations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the challenge of real-space imaging to presenting NV spectroscopy measurements on YIG (scatterer effects) and then tackling the complexity of LSMO stripe domains, culminating in detailed simulation comparisons.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum sensing (NV centers) with condensed matter magnetism, providing spatially resolved dynamics crucial for understanding how local magnetic structure dictates wave propagation—a key area for designing functional spintronic devices.

NV sensing of materials.note: The core methodology—using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spectroscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations to map local magnetic fields and spin-wave phase structure in magnetic films—is a direct extension of using NV centers to probe the magnetic properties of condensed matter systems.
